images.title: A quarter turn of a rangoli
images.purpose: Show that a rangoli with 4 equal petals looks the same after a quarter turn of 90 degrees.
images.composition: Two rangolis side by side with wide space between them and one turning arrow between them.
images.exact_structure: Left: a round rangoli with a small centre ring and 4 equal petals at the top, right, bottom and left, teal #0072B2. Right: the same rangoli after a quarter turn, looking exactly the same. Between them one curved reddish purple #CC79A7 arrow showing a turn about the centre. Exactly 2 rangolis, 4 petals each, 1 arrow.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
petals of different size or uneven spacing
images.takeaway: A turn of 90 degrees brings the rangoli onto itself.
images.description: Two identical teal rangolis with 4 petals around a ring, joined by a curved arrow marked 90 degrees.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to say why the picture looks the same after the quarter turn.

image_decisions.why: The idea is a picture idea; one clean image carries it.
